facts: Healing is a process by which the body repairs damaged tissue.
Cells work together to fix injuries over time.
Sometimes damaged tissue is replaced with healthy tissue of the same kind.
Sometimes damaged tissue is replaced with scar tissue instead.
false_claims: Healing means damaged tissue never changes.
notes: Reviewed: split colon-style bullet into two scorable facts.

facts: The International English Language Testing System (IELTS) measures English fluency.
Test takers choose the Academic Module or the General Training Module.
The Academic Module is for people applying to university.
The General Training Module is for work, training, or immigration.
false_claims: IELTS tests only mathematics skills.
notes: Reviewed: domain=other; consolidated redundant module facts.

facts: Ink is a liquid that is used to write, draw, print, or make marks.
Ink is used in pens, in some computer printers, and in printing presses.
In some countries, people write by using ink and brushes.
People usually write or print using black ink, but ink can be any color.
The first ink was used in Egypt about 2600 BC.
false_claims: Ink is a solid metal used only in factories.
notes: Reviewed: added rater trap; facts unchanged.

facts: The inch is a unit of length in the Imperial and U.S. customary systems.
Inches are written as in or with the double-prime symbol.
There are 12 inches in one foot.
One inch equals 2.54 centimeters.
false_claims: One foot equals 12 centimeters.
notes: Reviewed: clarified abbreviation wording after broken extraction.

facts: An insult is words that offend or hurt someone.
An insult may or may not be true.
Insults are a form of derogatory language.
Words like foolish or stupid insult a person's intelligence.
false_claims: An insult is always a true statement of fact.
notes: Reviewed: shortened long bullet; domain=everyday.

facts: The kilometre is a common unit for longer distances on Earth.
One kilometre equals 1,000 metres.
Most countries use kilometres for road and sea distances.
The UK and USA often use miles instead of kilometres for roads.
false_claims: One kilometre equals 100 metres.
notes: Batch 2 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed weak claims, added false_claims where missing; approved for promote.

facts: A leap year is a calendar year with an extra day in the Gregorian calendar.
A common year has 365 days, but a leap year has 366 days.
The extra day is February 29, added to the month of February.
Leap years help keep the calendar aligned with Earth's orbit around the Sun.
false_claims: Every year is a leap year.
notes: Batch 2 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed weak claims, added false_claims where missing; approved for promote.

facts: A microscope is a scientific instrument that makes small objects look larger.
Microscopes let people see tiny things that are hard to see with the naked eye.
Doctors and scientists often use microscopes in their work.
Students use microscopes in biology classes to study small specimens.
Compound microscopes use at least two lenses.
false_claims: A microscope makes large objects look smaller.
notes: Batch 2 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed weak claims, added false_claims where missing; approved for promote.

facts: Physiology is the study of how living things and their parts function.
Physiology examines how organs and systems work inside the body.
Human physiology helps explain breathing, digestion, and movement.
Physiologists study healthy bodies and how disease changes them.
false_claims: Physiology only studies plants, not animals.
notes: Batch 2 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed weak claims, added false_claims where missing; approved for promote.

facts: Skin is the outer covering of the human body and many animals.
Skin protects the body from germs, water loss, and injury.
Skin helps control body temperature through sweat and blood flow.
Skin contains nerves that let us feel touch, heat, and pain.
false_claims: Skin has nothing to do with feeling touch.
notes: Batch 2 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed weak claims, added false_claims where missing; approved for promote.

facts: A simile is a figure of speech that compares two things using like or as.
An example is: her smile was like sunshine.
Similes help writers paint vivid pictures in the reader's mind.
Similes are common in poetry and everyday speech.
false_claims: A simile compares things without using like or as.
notes: Batch 2 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed weak claims, added false_claims where missing; approved for promote.

facts: Soap is a substance used for washing hands, skin, and clothes.
Soap mixes with water to help remove dirt and oil.
Bar soap and liquid soap are common forms.
Washing with soap helps reduce the spread of germs.
false_claims: Soap is only used for cooking food.
notes: Batch 2 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed weak claims, added false_claims where missing; approved for promote.

facts: A zebra is an African wild animal related to horses and donkeys.
Zebras are known for their black and white stripes.
Each zebra's stripe pattern is unique.
Zebras live in grasslands and savannas in Africa.
false_claims: Zebras have spots instead of stripes.
notes: Batch 2 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed weak claims, added false_claims where missing; approved for promote.

facts: Asia is the largest continent on Earth by area and population.
Asia stretches from the Middle East to Japan and from Russia to Indonesia.
More than half of the world's people live in Asia.
Asia includes many countries, cultures, and languages.
false_claims: Asia is the smallest continent.
notes: Batch 2 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed weak claims, added false_claims where missing; approved for promote.

facts: The North Pole is the northernmost point on Earth.
The North Pole lies in the Arctic Ocean, where ice covers the sea.
The North Pole has six months of daylight and six months of darkness.
Explorers and scientists have traveled to the North Pole.
false_claims: The North Pole is on the continent of Antarctica.
notes: Batch 2 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed weak claims, added false_claims where missing; approved for promote.

facts: Argon is a chemical element.
The symbol for argon is Ar, and its atomic number is 18.
Argon belongs to the noble gas group.
Argon is an odorless and tasteless gas.
Argon is the third-most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere.
false_claims: Argon is a metal that rusts in water.
notes: Batch 3 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed domains/claims, added false_claims; approved for promote.

facts: A carnivore is an animal that eats mainly or only meat.
Predators often hunt and kill their own prey.
Scavengers are carnivores that eat animals they did not kill themselves.
Carnivores that eat mainly insects are called insectivores.
Carnivores that eat mainly fish are called piscivores.
false_claims: A carnivore is an animal that eats only plants.
notes: Batch 3 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed domains/claims, added false_claims; approved for promote.

facts: Senegal is a country in West Africa.
Senegal covers a land area of almost 197,000 square kilometres.
Senegal has a tropical climate with a dry season and a rainy season.
Senegal gained independence from France in 1960.
false_claims: Senegal is a country in northern Europe.
notes: Batch 3 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed domains/claims, added false_claims; approved for promote.

facts: HTML is a markup language used to create web pages.
HTML was created in 1990 by Tim Berners-Lee.
Web pages can include writing, links, pictures, sound, and video.
HTML tells web browsers how pages should look.
HTML can also store meta information about a page, such as who created it.
false_claims: HTML is a language spoken only in France.
notes: Batch 3 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed domains/claims, added false_claims; approved for promote.

facts: The Missouri River is a river in the western United States.
The Missouri River is a tributary of the Mississippi River.
The Missouri River is longer than the Mississippi River.
The Missouri River is the longest river in North America.
false_claims: The Missouri River is the shortest river in Asia.
notes: Batch 3 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed domains/claims, added false_claims; approved for promote.

facts: A day is the time it takes Earth to spin around once.
Daytime happens on the side of Earth facing the Sun.
Nighttime happens on the side of Earth facing away from the Sun.
One full spin takes about 24 hours, including day and night.
false_claims: A day is the time it takes Earth to orbit the Moon once.
notes: Batch 3 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed domains/claims, added false_claims; approved for promote.

facts: An airport is a place where airplanes can land and take off.
Most airports have a long level strip called a runway.
A terminal is a building where passengers wait for planes or luggage.
Hangars store planes when they are not in use.
A control tower helps guide planes safely around the airport.
false_claims: An airport is a place where only trains stop underground.
notes: Batch 3 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed domains/claims, added false_claims; approved for promote.

facts: Summer is one of the four seasons.
Summer is usually the hottest season of the year.
In some places summer is wet, and in other places it is dry.
Summer happens in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres at opposite times of the year.
false_claims: Summer is always the coldest season everywhere on Earth.
notes: Batch 3 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed domains/claims, added false_claims; approved for promote.

facts: Percent means out of one hundred.
Percent is often shown with the symbol %.
Percent can be used even when there are not exactly one hundred items.
Percent is also used to show how amounts change.
false_claims: Percent means out of two only.
notes: Batch 3 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed domains/claims, added false_claims; approved for promote.

facts: A sundial shows the time during the day using the Sun.
As the Sun moves across the sky, a shadow falls on different parts of the dial.
Marks on the dial show what time a certain shadow means.
A common design is the horizontal garden sundial.
false_claims: A sundial only works underwater at midnight.
notes: Batch 3 QA pass: subject-first bullets, fixed domains/claims, added false_claims; approved for promote.
